# ==============================================================================
# 5. ATTRIBUTE EXTRACTION
# ==============================================================================

extract_silix_attribute <- function(
  attribute_string,
  attribute_name
) {

  pattern <- paste0(
    "(?:^|;)",
    attribute_name,
    "=([^;]+)"
  )

  extracted_value <- sub(
    paste0(
      ".*",
      pattern,
      ".*"
    ),
    "\\1",
    as.character(
      attribute_string
    ),
    perl = TRUE
  )

  no_match <- !grepl(
    pattern,
    as.character(
      attribute_string
    ),
    perl = TRUE
  )

  extracted_value[no_match] <- NA_character_

  extracted_value
}

# ==============================================================================
# 10. READ SETARIA 5′ LTR ASSIGNMENTS
#
# Setaria uses more than one full-sequence ID convention.
#
# Examples:
#
# lLTR_RLCSvm1G00294 -> RLCSvm1G00294
# lLTR_RLGSvm1G00234 -> RLGSvm1G00234
# lLTR_RLXSvm1G00072 -> LTRRT_RLXSvm1G00072
#
# Candidate 1 = remove lLTR_
# Candidate 2 = remove lLTR_ and prepend LTRRT_
#
# The candidate that actually exists in the full-sequence file is retained.
# ==============================================================================

setaria_five_raw <- data.table::fread(
  setaria_5prime_path,
  header = FALSE,
  sep = "\t",
  select = 1:2,
  col.names = c(
    "Five_Family_ID",
    "Five_Element_Attributes"
  )
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    Five_Prime_LTR_ID = extract_silix_attribute(
      Five_Element_Attributes,
      "ID"
    ),

    Five_Prime_Family = paste0(
      "Setaria_5prime_",
      Five_Family_ID
    )
  )


full_setaria_ids <- unique(
  setaria_full_with_id$TE_ID
)


setaria_five_with_id <- setaria_five_raw %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(Five_Prime_LTR_ID)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    Candidate_TE_ID_1 = sub(
      "^lLTR_",
      "",
      Five_Prime_LTR_ID
    ),

    Candidate_TE_ID_2 = paste0(
      "LTRRT_",
      Candidate_TE_ID_1
    ),

    Candidate_1_Matches =
      Candidate_TE_ID_1 %in%
      full_setaria_ids,

    Candidate_2_Matches =
      Candidate_TE_ID_2 %in%
      full_setaria_ids,

    TE_ID = dplyr::case_when(

      Candidate_1_Matches &
        !Candidate_2_Matches ~
        Candidate_TE_ID_1,

      Candidate_2_Matches &
        !Candidate_1_Matches ~
        Candidate_TE_ID_2,

      Candidate_1_Matches &
        Candidate_2_Matches ~
        Candidate_TE_ID_1,

      TRUE ~
        NA_character_
    )
  )

          !Candidate_2_Matches,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    LTRRT_Prefix_Matches =
      sum(
        Candidate_2_Matches &
          !Candidate_1_Matches,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    Both_Candidates_Match =
      sum(
        Candidate_1_Matches &

    No_Match =

        is.na(TE_ID)

# ==============================================================================
# 12. CLASSIFY INDIVIDUAL TEs
#
# Final individual-TE definition — SAME AS FIGURE 1 PANEL C:
#
# A TE is concordant when its full-sequence / 5′ LTR family pair is the
# UNIQUE largest overlap for BOTH the full-sequence family and 5′ LTR family.
#
# All other TEs are discordant.
# ==============================================================================

classify_individual_te_status <- function(
  assignment_df,
  species_name
) {

  clean_assignments <- assignment_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(TE_ID),
      !is.na(Full_Seq_Family),
      !is.na(Five_Prime_Family)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(
      TE_ID,
      .keep_all = TRUE
    )

  pair_counts <- clean_assignments %>%
    dplyr::count(
      Full_Seq_Family,
      Five_Prime_Family,
      name = "Pair_Size"
    )

  pair_classification <- pair_counts %>%
    dplyr::group_by(
      Full_Seq_Family
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(

      Largest_Pair_in_Full =
        max(Pair_Size),

      Number_Tied_for_Full_Max =
        sum(
          Pair_Size ==
            Largest_Pair_in_Full
        ),

      Unique_Full_Maximum =
        Pair_Size ==
          Largest_Pair_in_Full &
        Number_Tied_for_Full_Max ==
          1
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::group_by(
      Five_Prime_Family
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(

      Largest_Pair_in_Five =
        max(Pair_Size),

      Number_Tied_for_Five_Max =
        sum(
          Pair_Size ==
            Largest_Pair_in_Five
        ),

      Unique_Five_Maximum =
        Pair_Size ==
          Largest_Pair_in_Five &
        Number_Tied_for_Five_Max ==
          1
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(

      Mutual_Unique_Largest =
        Unique_Full_Maximum &
        Unique_Five_Maximum,

      Clustering_Status =
        dplyr::if_else(
          Mutual_Unique_Largest,
          "Clustering concordance",
          "Clustering discordance"
        )
    )

  clean_assignments %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      pair_classification,
      by = c(
        "Full_Seq_Family",
        "Five_Prime_Family"
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(

      Species = species_name,

      Clustering_Status = factor(
        Clustering_Status,
        levels = c(
          "Clustering concordance",
          "Clustering discordance"
        )
      )
    )
}

# ==============================================================================
# 13. PANEL A — REBUILD THE DATA EXACTLY AS IN THE ORIGINAL JACCARD ANALYSIS
#
# IMPORTANT:
# Panel A in the original analysis did NOT use the TE_ID tables used later for
# the age and superfamily analyses.
#
# It used read_silix_assignments(), which:
#   1. extracts Name= from each SiLiX record,
#   2. de-duplicates by TE_Name within each clustering method,
#   3. joins full-sequence and 5′ LTR assignments by TE_Name.
#
# This distinction is why the previous standalone versions produced the wrong
# Maize distribution and the wrong sample size.
# ==============================================================================


parse_te_name <- function(element_id_vector) {

  sub(
    ".*Name=([^;]+).*",
    "\\1",
    element_id_vector
  )
}


read_silix_assignments_for_jaccard <- function(
  full_path,
  five_prime_path,
  species_name
) {

  full_dt <- data.table::fread(
    full_path,
    header = FALSE,
    sep = "\t",
    select = 1:2,
    col.names = c(
      "Family_ID",
      "Element_ID"
    )
  )

  five_prime_dt <- data.table::fread(
    five_prime_path,
    header = FALSE,
    sep = "\t",
    select = 1:2,
    col.names = c(
      "Family_ID",
      "Element_ID"
    )
  )


  full_families <- full_dt %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      TE_Name =
        parse_te_name(
          Element_ID
        ),

      Full_Seq_Family =
        paste0(
          species_name,
          "_Full_",
          Family_ID
        )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(
      TE_Name,
      .keep_all = TRUE
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      TE_Name,
      Full_Seq_Family
    )


  five_prime_families <- five_prime_dt %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      TE_Name =
        parse_te_name(
          Element_ID
        ),

      Five_Prime_Family =
        paste0(
          species_name,
          "_5prime_",
          Family_ID
        )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(
      TE_Name,
      .keep_all = TRUE
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      TE_Name,
      Five_Prime_Family
    )


  merged_df <- dplyr::inner_join(
    full_families,
    five_prime_families,
    by = "TE_Name"
  ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Species =
        species_name
    )


  if(
    nrow(
      merged_df
    ) == 0
  ) {

    stop(
      "No shared TE names were found for ",
      species_name,
      "."
    )
  }


  merged_df
}

  read_silix_assignments_for_jaccard(

    five_prime_path =

# ==============================================================================
# 14. CALCULATE JACCARD FOR EVERY OVERLAPPING FAMILY PAIR
#
# This is the original family-membership Jaccard calculation:
#
#                        shared TEs
# Jaccard = -----------------------------------------
#           full family + 5′ family - shared TEs
# ==============================================================================


calculate_family_jaccard_original <- function(
  assignment_df
) {

  pair_counts <- assignment_df %>%
    dplyr::count(
      Species,
      Full_Seq_Family,
      Five_Prime_Family,
      name =
        "Shared_TEs"
    )


  full_sizes <- assignment_df %>%
    dplyr::count(
      Species,
      Full_Seq_Family,
      name =
        "Full_Family_Size"
    )


  five_sizes <- assignment_df %>%
    dplyr::count(
      Species,
      Five_Prime_Family,
      name =
        "Five_Prime_Family_Size"
    )


  pair_counts %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      full_sizes,
      by = c(
        "Species",
        "Full_Seq_Family"
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      five_sizes,
      by = c(
        "Species",
        "Five_Prime_Family"
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(

      Union_TEs =
        Full_Family_Size +
        Five_Prime_Family_Size -
        Shared_TEs,

      Jaccard_Similarity =
        Shared_TEs /
        Union_TEs
    )
}


jaccard_df_all <-
  calculate_family_jaccard_original(
    combined_jaccard_elements
  )


# ==============================================================================
# 15. IDENTIFY DISCORDANT FAMILY RELATIONSHIPS
#
# This reproduces the ORIGINAL connected-component code used for the plot on
# Slide 2.
#
# Each family is a node in a bipartite graph:
#   full-sequence family <-> 5′ LTR family
#
# A connected component containing exactly one family from each method is
# concordant.
#
# Any component containing more than one family on either side is discordant.
# ==============================================================================


build_original_topology <- function(
  assignment_df
) {

  topology_edges <- assignment_df %>%
    dplyr::count(
      Species,
      Full_Seq_Family,
      Five_Prime_Family,
      name =
        "Pair_Size"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(

      Full_Node =
        paste0(
          Species,
          "::FULL::",
          Full_Seq_Family
        ),

      Five_Node =
        paste0(
          Species,
          "::FIVE::",
          Five_Prime_Family
        )
    )


  graph_object <-
    igraph::graph_from_data_frame(
      topology_edges %>%
        dplyr::select(
          Full_Node,
          Five_Node
        ),
      directed = FALSE
    )


  graph_components <-
    igraph::components(
      graph_object
    )


  node_components <-
    tibble::tibble(

      Node =
        names(
          graph_components$membership
        ),

      Component_ID =
        as.integer(
          graph_components$membership
        )
    )


  topology_edges <-
    topology_edges %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      node_components,
      by = c(
        "Full_Node" =
          "Node"
      )
    )


  component_topology <-
    topology_edges %>%
    dplyr::group_by(
      Species,
      Component_ID
    ) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(

      Number_Full_Families =
        dplyr::n_distinct(
          Full_Seq_Family
        ),

      Number_Five_Families =
        dplyr::n_distinct(
          Five_Prime_Family
        ),

      Topology =
        dplyr::case_when(

          Number_Full_Families == 1 &
            Number_Five_Families == 1 ~
            "Concordant",

          Number_Full_Families == 1 &
            Number_Five_Families > 1 ~
            "Split-associated",

          Number_Full_Families > 1 &
            Number_Five_Families == 1 ~
            "Merge-associated",

          Number_Full_Families > 1 &
            Number_Five_Families > 1 ~
            "Split-and-merge",

          TRUE ~
            "Other"
        ),

      .groups =
        "drop"
    )


  list(
    edges =
      topology_edges,

    components =
      component_topology
  )
}


original_topology <-
  build_original_topology(
    combined_jaccard_elements
  )


topology_edges <-
  original_topology$edges


component_topology <-
  original_topology$components


discordant_components <-
  component_topology %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Topology !=
      "Concordant"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Species,
    Component_ID,
    Topology
  )


# ==============================================================================
# 16. ATTACH TOPOLOGY TO JACCARD PAIRS AND RETAIN DISCORDANT RELATIONSHIPS
#
# This block is copied from the logic in the original script.
# ==============================================================================


jaccard_with_topology <-
  jaccard_df_all %>%

  dplyr::left_join(

    topology_edges %>%
      dplyr::select(
        Species,
        Full_Seq_Family,
        Five_Prime_Family,
        Component_ID
      ) %>%
      dplyr::distinct(),

    by = c(
      "Species",
      "Full_Seq_Family",
      "Five_Prime_Family"
    )
  ) %>%

  dplyr::left_join(

    discordant_components,

    by = c(
      "Species",
      "Component_ID"
    )
  )


discordant_jaccard_df <-
  jaccard_with_topology %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(
      Topology
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Species =
      factor(
        Species,
        levels = c(
          "B73",
          "Setaria"
        )
      )
  )


# ==============================================================================
# 16A. ORIGINAL SLIDE-2 CHECK
#
# The Slide 2 plot supplied with the manuscript has:
#
#   Maize   n = 887
#   Setaria n = 112
#
# The original Jaccard workflow must reproduce those values.
# ==============================================================================


panel_a_counts <-
  discordant_jaccard_df %>%
  dplyr::count(
    Species,
    name = "n"
  )


print(
  panel_a_counts,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)


expected_panel_a_counts <-
  tibble::tibble(

    Species =
      factor(
        c(
          "B73",
          "Setaria"
        ),
        levels = c(
          "B73",
          "Setaria"
        )
      ),

    Expected_n =
      c(
        887L,
        112L
      )
  )


panel_a_count_check <-
  panel_a_counts %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    expected_panel_a_counts,
    by = "Species"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Matches_Slide_2 =
      n ==
      Expected_n
  )


print(
  panel_a_count_check,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)


if(
  any(
    !panel_a_count_check$Matches_Slide_2
  )
) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "\nPANEL A DOES NOT MATCH THE ORIGINAL SLIDE 2 DATA.\n",
      "Expected: Maize n = 887; Setaria n = 112.\n",
      "The script has stopped instead of drawing the wrong Panel A.\n",
      "Please send the printed panel_a_count_check table."
    )
  )
}


# ==============================================================================
# 16B. PANEL A SUMMARY + MEAN LABELS
# ==============================================================================


jaccard_summary <-
  discordant_jaccard_df %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    Species
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(

    n =
      dplyr::n(),

    Mean_Jaccard =
      mean(
        Jaccard_Similarity,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    Median_Jaccard =
      median(
        Jaccard_Similarity,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups =
      "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    n_label =
      paste0(
        "n = ",
        scales::comma(
          n
        )
      ),

    mean_label =
      paste0(
        "Mean = ",
        sprintf(
          "%.2f",
          Mean_Jaccard
        )
      )
  )


# ==============================================================================
# 16C. PANEL A — MATCH SLIDE 2 APPEARANCE
#
# Slide 2:
#   Maize   = green  #1B9E77
#   Setaria = coral  #D55E6A
#
# Mean labels are the only addition requested relative to the original slide.
# ==============================================================================


pA <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  discordant_jaccard_df,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = Species,
    y = Jaccard_Similarity,
    fill = Species
  )
) +

  ggplot2::geom_violin(
    trim = TRUE,
    scale = "width",
    alpha = 0.75,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.12,
    fill = "white",
    outlier.shape = NA,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.45
  ) +

  ggplot2::stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    shape = 23,
    size = 2.5,
    fill = "white",
    color = "black"
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data =
      jaccard_summary,

    ggplot2::aes(
      x = Species,
      y = 1.045,
      label = n_label
    ),

    inherit.aes =
      FALSE,

    size =
      2.8,

    color =
      "black"
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data =
      jaccard_summary,

    ggplot2::aes(
      x = Species,
      y = 0.995,
      label = mean_label
    ),

    inherit.aes =
      FALSE,

    size =
      2.8,

    fontface =
      "bold",

    color =
      "black"
  ) +

  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "B73" =
        divergent_palette[2],
      "Setaria" =
        divergent_palette[6]
    )
  ) +

  ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(
    labels = c(
      "B73" =
        "Maize",
      "Setaria" =
        "Setaria"
    )
  ) +

  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(
      0,
      1.08
    ),
    breaks = seq(
      0,
      1,
      0.25
    ),
    expand = c(
      0,
      0
    )
  ) +

  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Jaccard similarity"
  ) +

  publication_theme +

  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position =
      "none"
  )


# ==============================================================================
# 17. PANEL B DATA — LTR IDENTITY
#
# LTR identity comes directly from the full-sequence SiLiX attributes used in
# the original age analysis.
# ==============================================================================

age_df <- combined_te_status %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(LTR_Identity)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Species = factor(
      Species,
      levels = c(
        "B73",
        "Setaria"
      )
    ),
    Clustering_Status = factor(
      Clustering_Status,
      levels = c(
        "Clustering concordance",
        "Clustering discordance"
      )
    )
  )


age_summary <- age_df %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    Species,
    Clustering_Status
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(

    n =
      dplyr::n_distinct(
        TE_ID
      ),

    Mean_LTR_Identity =
      mean(
        LTR_Identity,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    n_label = paste0(
      "n = ",
      scales::comma(n)
    ),

    mean_label = paste0(
      "Mean = ",
      sprintf(
        "%.3f",
        Mean_LTR_Identity
      )
    )
  )


# ==============================================================================
# 18. PANEL B — LTR IDENTITY
# ==============================================================================

age_y_min <- floor(
  min(
    age_df$LTR_Identity,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) * 20
) / 20


pB <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  age_df,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = Clustering_Status,
    y = LTR_Identity,
    fill = Clustering_Status
  )
) +

  ggplot2::geom_violin(
    trim = TRUE,
    alpha = 0.78,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.45
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.12,
    fill = "white",
    outlier.shape = NA,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.45
  ) +

  ggplot2::stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    shape = 23,
    size = 2.5,
    fill = "white",
    color = "black"
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data = age_summary,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = Clustering_Status,
      y = 1.016,
      label = n_label
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 2.5
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data = age_summary,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = Clustering_Status,
      y = 0.998,
      label = mean_label
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 2.4,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +

  ggplot2::facet_wrap(
    ~Species,
    nrow = 1,
    labeller = ggplot2::as_labeller(
      c(
        "B73" = "Maize",
        "Setaria" = "Setaria"
      )
    )
  ) +

  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = status_colors
  ) +

  ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(
    labels = c(
      "Clustering concordance" =
        "Concordant",
      "Clustering discordance" =
        "Discordant"
    )
  ) +

  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(
      age_y_min,
      1.03
    ),
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(
      mult = c(
        0.01,
        0
      )
    )
  ) +

  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "LTR identity"
  ) +

  publication_theme +

  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "none",

      size = 8
    ),

      0.45,
      "cm"
    )
  )


# ==============================================================================
# 19. PANEL C DATA — SUPERFAMILY
#
# This follows the ORIGINAL enrichment analysis:
#
# Relative enrichment =
#
#     proportion of discordant TEs in superfamily
#     --------------------------------------------
#     genome-wide proportion of TEs in superfamily
#
# Classification is taken directly from the same full-sequence records used
# for the TE assignments.
# ==============================================================================

te_superfamily_status <- combined_te_status %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Species,
    TE_ID,
    Clustering_Status,
    Classification
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    Species,
    TE_ID,
    .keep_all = TRUE
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    LTR_Superfamily =
      dplyr::case_when(

        grepl(
          "Copia",
          Classification,
          ignore.case = TRUE
        ) ~
          "Ty1/Copia",

        grepl(
          "Gypsy|Ty3",
          Classification,
          ignore.case = TRUE
        ) ~
          "Ty3",

        grepl(
          "LTR",
          Classification,
          ignore.case = TRUE
        ) ~
          "Other",

        TRUE ~
          NA_character_
      ),

    Discordant =
      dplyr::if_else(
        Clustering_Status ==
          "Clustering discordance",
        1L,
        0L
      )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(LTR_Superfamily),
    !is.na(Discordant)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    Species = factor(
      Species,
      levels = c(
        "B73",
        "Setaria"
      )
    ),

    LTR_Superfamily = factor(
      LTR_Superfamily,
      levels = c(
        "Ty1/Copia",
        "Ty3",
        "Other"
      )
    )
  )


# ==============================================================================
# 20. PANEL C — GENOME-WIDE SUPERFAMILY COMPOSITION
# ==============================================================================

genomewide_superfamily <- te_superfamily_status %>%
  dplyr::count(
    Species,
    LTR_Superfamily,
    name = "Genomewide_Number_of_TEs"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    Species
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    Genomewide_Total_TEs =
      sum(
        Genomewide_Number_of_TEs
      ),

    Genomewide_Proportion =
      Genomewide_Number_of_TEs /
      Genomewide_Total_TEs
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()


# ==============================================================================
# 21. PANEL C — DISCORDANT SUPERFAMILY COMPOSITION
# ==============================================================================

discordant_superfamily <- te_superfamily_status %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Discordant == 1
  ) %>%
  dplyr::count(
    Species,
    LTR_Superfamily,
    name = "Discordant_Number_of_TEs"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    Species
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    Total_Discordant_TEs =
      sum(
        Discordant_Number_of_TEs
      ),

    Discordant_Proportion =
      Discordant_Number_of_TEs /
      Total_Discordant_TEs
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()


# ==============================================================================
# 22. PANEL C — RELATIVE ENRICHMENT
# ==============================================================================

superfamily_enrichment <- genomewide_superfamily %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    discordant_superfamily,
    by = c(
      "Species",
      "LTR_Superfamily"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    Discordant_Number_of_TEs =
      tidyr::replace_na(
        Discordant_Number_of_TEs,
        0L
      ),

    Discordant_Proportion =
      tidyr::replace_na(
        Discordant_Proportion,
        0
      ),

    Relative_Enrichment =
      Discordant_Proportion /
      Genomewide_Proportion,

    Enrichment_Deviation =
      Relative_Enrichment -
      1,

    Enrichment_Label =
      paste0(
        sprintf(
          "%.2f",
          Relative_Enrichment
        ),
        "×"
      ),

    Label_Y =
      dplyr::if_else(
        Enrichment_Deviation >= 0,
        Enrichment_Deviation + 0.07,
        Enrichment_Deviation - 0.07
      )
  )


# ==============================================================================
# 23. PANEL C — DIVERGING ENRICHMENT PLOT
#
# Relative enrichment = 1 is the null expectation.
#
# For display:
#
#   Relative enrichment - 1
#
# Therefore:
#   > 0 = enriched
#   < 0 = depleted
# ==============================================================================

panel_c_lower <- min(
  c(
    superfamily_enrichment$Enrichment_Deviation,
    superfamily_enrichment$Label_Y
  ),
  na.rm = TRUE
) - 0.10


panel_c_upper <- max(
  c(
    superfamily_enrichment$Enrichment_Deviation,
    superfamily_enrichment$Label_Y
  ),
  na.rm = TRUE
) + 0.10


pC <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  superfamily_enrichment,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = LTR_Superfamily,
    y = Enrichment_Deviation,
    fill = LTR_Superfamily
  )
) +

  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.6,
    color = "black"
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_col(
    width = 0.65,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.45
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_text(
    ggplot2::aes(
      y = Label_Y,
      label = Enrichment_Label
    ),
    size = 3.1,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "black"
  ) +

  ggplot2::facet_wrap(
    ~Species,
    nrow = 1,
    labeller = ggplot2::as_labeller(
      c(
        "B73" = "Maize",
        "Setaria" = "Setaria"
      )
    )
  ) +

  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = superfamily_colors,
    drop = FALSE
  ) +

  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(
      panel_c_lower,
      panel_c_upper
    ),
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(
      n = 5
    ),
    expand = c(
      0,
      0
    )
  ) +

  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "LTR superfamily",
    y = "Relative enrichment\namong discordant TEs"
  ) +

  publication_theme +

  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.spacing.x = grid::unit(
      0.45,
      "cm"
    ),
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(
      size = 8.5
    )
  )


# ==============================================================================
# 24. ASSEMBLE FIGURE 2
# ==============================================================================

figure2 <- pA / pB / pC +

  patchwork::plot_layout(
    heights = c(
      0.90,
      1.08,
      1.05
    )
  ) +

  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    tag_levels = "A"
  ) &

  ggplot2::theme(
    plot.tag = ggplot2::element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 12
    ),
    plot.tag.position = c(
      0.01,
      0.99
    ),
    plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(
      4,
      6,
      6,
      6
    )
  )


# ==============================================================================
# 25. SAVE FIGURE
# ==============================================================================

ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    output_dir,
    "Figure2_full_panel_FINAL.jpeg"
  ),
  plot = figure2,
  width = 7.6,
  height = 9.0,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)


ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    output_dir,
    "Figure2_full_panel_FINAL.pdf"
  ),
  plot = figure2,
  width = 7.6,
  height = 9.0,
  units = "in",
  bg = "white"
)


# ==============================================================================
# 26. VALIDATION OUTPUT
# ==============================================================================

cat(
  "\n\n============================================================\n",
  "INPUT / ID CHECKS\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)

cat(
  "B73 full-sequence TEs: ",
  dplyr::n_distinct(
    b73_full_with_id$TE_ID
  ),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)

cat(
  "B73 5′ LTR TEs: ",
  dplyr::n_distinct(
    b73_five_with_id$TE_ID
  ),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)

cat(
  "B73 matched TEs: ",
  dplyr::n_distinct(
    b73_assignments$TE_ID
  ),
  "\n\n",
  sep = ""
)

cat(
  "Setaria full-sequence TEs: ",
  dplyr::n_distinct(
    setaria_full_with_id$TE_ID
  ),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)

cat(
  "Setaria recovered 5′ LTR TEs: ",
  dplyr::n_distinct(
    setaria_five_with_id$TE_ID
  ),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)

cat(
  "Setaria matched TEs: ",
  dplyr::n_distinct(
    setaria_assignments$TE_ID
  ),
  "\n\n",
  sep = ""
)

cat(
  "Setaria ID recovery:\n"
)

print(
  setaria_id_recovery_summary,
  width = Inf
)


cat(
  "\n\n============================================================\n",
  "PANEL A — JACCARD\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)

print(
  jaccard_summary,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)


cat(
  "\n\n============================================================\n",
  "PANEL B — LTR IDENTITY\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)

print(
  age_summary,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)


cat(
  "\n\n============================================================\n",
  "PANEL C — GENOME-WIDE SUPERFAMILY COMPOSITION\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)

print(
  genomewide_superfamily,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)


cat(
  "\n\n============================================================\n",
  "PANEL C — DISCORDANT SUPERFAMILY COMPOSITION\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)

print(
  discordant_superfamily,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)


cat(
  "\n\n============================================================\n",
  "PANEL C — RELATIVE ENRICHMENT\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)

print(
  superfamily_enrichment %>%
    dplyr::select(
      Species,
      LTR_Superfamily,
      Genomewide_Number_of_TEs,
      Genomewide_Proportion,
      Discordant_Number_of_TEs,
      Discordant_Proportion,
      Relative_Enrichment,
      Enrichment_Deviation
    ),
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)


cat(
  "\nExpected approximate Slide 2 Panel C values:\n",
  "Maize:   Ty1/Copia 0.62× | Ty3 1.31× | Other 0.91×\n",
  "Setaria: Ty1/Copia 0.83× | Ty3 0.77× | Other 2.45×\n\n",
  sep = ""
)


# ==============================================================================
# 27. SHOW FIGURE
# ==============================================================================

print(
  figure2
)
